# Roadmap: SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | A uv workspace whose members are the four `packages/*` scaffolds.

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A historical baseline of quarterly filing indexes for a chosen quarter range | §3 R1; §2.1, §4.2 | A | 1 | Requests are small: at most about 136 quarterly files (1993 Q1 to 2026 Q4, if the full range is chosen), which takes under a minute at the 3 req/s target (§4.8). Bytes per quarter are measured by Stage 1. |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2; §2.1, §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year (business days), so the request count is negligible. File size is measured by Stage 1. |
| O3 | One canonical, deduplicated filing-index dataset in Parquet, with provenance, built from those indexes | §3 R3; §4.4, §4.5, §4.6 | A | 3 | Compute is measured by Stage 1 (§7 step 4 names the figures to record). |
| O4 | The pipeline running in Azure: ADF orchestrating, Container Apps Jobs running the Python, ADLS for files, Table Storage for state, Azure Monitor for evidence | §3 R4; §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated before deployment; it is measured by Stage 6's smoke test. |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs using the same downloader, parser and publisher | §3 R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Not material |
| O6 | Original index bytes kept, so a parser change reprocesses them with no new download | §3 R6; §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage equals the raw bytes of the chosen range, plus observation Parquet. Measured per quarter by Stage 1. |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read on a schedule, with additions and field changes reflected in the catalog | §3 R7; §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | Each run re-reads every supported quarter: up to about 136 requests plus their bytes, once a week. |
| O8 | All SEC traffic held to one shared request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | Not material |
| O9 | Readers find the current data for each quarter through one versioned pointer, and never by scanning files | §3 R9; §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | Not material |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only after an approval tied to the source hash, and never because of a failure or an absence | §3 R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your time: one review for each gated closed-quarter candidate |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

- Package placement. §4.9 puts all the code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repo also holds
  scaffolds named `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, and the
  root `pyproject.toml` declares a script for a `sec_edgar` module that does not exist. Proposed
  default: Stage 1's brainstorming settles which packages carry the code, and records the decision.
- Acceptance. The spec and the ADR are both PROPOSED (§7 step 1). Proposed default: Stages 1–5 run
  locally and do not depend on R4. ADR acceptance is consumed by Stage 6.

## Stages

Order: this follows your ranking, with two exceptions. O3 ships alongside O1, because a baseline
is only usable once it is parsed. O4 (rank 4) moves to Stage 6, because the Azure deployment can
only host the shared code once that code exists.

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — one real quarter and one real daily index, locally
      Objective: Download one archived quarter and one published daily index from the SEC, keep their bytes, and produce canonical Parquet rows on a local machine.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (scaffolds only)
      Produces: a working local collect→parse→Parquet path over real files; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the chosen quarter's master index is downloaded and its bytes are stored. O3 — Parquet rows that meet the §4.5 row contract exist for both files, with duplicates collapsed. Cost — the findings file records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory and the observed request rate for the real run.
      Leaves out: manifests (Stage 3); traceability (Stage 3); point-in-time awareness (Stage 3); full validation suites (Stage 5); deployment (Stage 6); scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily discovery and the shared collector
      Objective: Add daily ingestion through the same commands as backfill, behind one throttled collector.
      Outcomes: O2, O5, O8
      Consumes: Stage 1's collect→parse→Parquet path
      Produces: `discover`/`collect`/`transform` commands shared by backfill and daily runs; one request budget
      Exit: O2 — a missed run and a quarter-boundary catch-up over fixtures pick up every pending file, and a failed listing does not advance the checkpoint. O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader and parser. O8 — concurrent collectors in a test never exceed the configured rate, with retries counted.
      Leaves out: manifests (Stage 3); full validation suites (Stage 5); deployment, including the Storage-backed lease (Stage 6); scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Manifest, replay and versioned publication
      Objective: Keep source state durable, replay stored bytes, and publish each quarter's generation through one pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's shared commands
      Produces: source/snapshot/processing manifests; quarter generations with a conditional active pointer; `publish`
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds output from stored bytes with SEC access disabled, and the logical rows are unchanged. O9 — crash-injection tests show readers only complete generations, resolved through the pointer.
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 5); deployment (Stage 6)
      Picks up: manifests, traceability, point-in-time awareness
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and apply their changes, gating any removal behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 3's manifests, generations and pointer
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow; change reports; withdrawal approval records
      Exit: O7 — a corrected-quarter fixture publishes its additions and field updates as a new generation with a change report. O10 — a removal fixture stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its hash, open-quarter absence withdraws nothing, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 5); scheduling (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Configuration and the full CI suite
      Objective: Validate the §4.8 settings before any I/O, and bring CI up to the §6 exit criteria.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stages 1–4's commands
      Produces: typed configuration (§4.9); golden fixtures across the chosen range; the §6 CI suite
      Exit: O11 — every §5 configuration error is refused before any network request, and every §6 CI exit criterion has a passing test.
      Leaves out: deployment (Stage 6)
      Picks up: full validation suites
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Azure platform, deployment and smoke test
      Objective: Deploy the shared image on ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage and Azure Monitor to an isolated environment, and pass the §7 Phase 1 gate.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: an accepted ADR; Stage 5's configuration and CI suite
      Produces: infrastructure under `infra/azure/` with pinned identities; alerts; runbooks (§8); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-6-findings.md
      Exit: O4 — the integration tests and the §7 steps 3–5 smoke test and replay pass in isolated Azure resources, with all triggers disabled. Cost — the findings file records the smoke run's figures and its Azure spend.
      Leaves out: scheduling (Stage 7)
      Picks up: deployment
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the backfill, catch daily ingestion up, enable the triggers, and accept on observed scheduled runs (§7 Phase 2).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (operational standard)
      Consumes: Stage 6's deployed environment and runbooks
      Produces: a release record (§7 Exit); a production baseline; enabled daily and weekly triggers
      Exit: O1 — every requested quarter is published, or the incomplete range is recorded as approved. O2 — scheduled daily runs show in their durable reports. O7 — one manual and one scheduled reconciliation have completed, with any gated candidates resolved.
      Leaves out: nothing
      Picks up: scheduling
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note (or, for a writing-plans stage, the plan header) carries:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11, and over each numbered spec
requirement that no outcome's `Spec` cell cites. Each verdict needs path:line or test-name
evidence and names the stage plan that built it. Each unmet item becomes a new stage or a
recorded deferral with its reason (SKILL.md §6).
